timeline: One dollar for every meter.
Sounds like nothing?
But you could already be a millionaire — just by living your life.
The average person takes about 6,000 steps a day.
That's 4.5 kilometers — 4,500 dollars.
In a year — over one and a half million.
The rules are simple.
Max and Sam get the same message: one dollar for every meter.
On foot only — cars, elevators and treadmills don't count.
Max takes off and walks all day and all night.
60 kilometers — 60,000 dollars in one day!
Sam calmly walks 25 kilometers and goes to bed.
On day two, Max squeezes out another 40.
He has 100,000, Sam has 50.
Max is already sending him screenshots.
But on day three, Max can't get up.
His feet are raw, his knees won't bend.
For two weeks — just 2 kilometers a day.
Then he recovers, but never risks it again — 10 kilometers a day.
And Sam keeps walking.
25 kilometers every day — in the rain, on weekends, with music in his ears.
And by day five, he passes Max.
A year goes by.
Max has 3.6 million.
Not bad.
But Sam has 9 million!
Two and a half times more.
Not because he was faster.
Because he never stopped.
And one last thing.
In 70 years, a person walks about 115,000 kilometers — almost three times around the Earth.
That's 115 million dollars.
Just for walking.
So would you sprint like Max, or walk like Sam?
